labels.label: A: silver bottle

labels.label: B: orange bottle

trials.review: Body color, cap shape, and printed branding agree with the previous identities even though positions changed. The orange bottle appears larger in this frame, but that does not change its identity.

labels.label: A: silver bottle
labels.evidence: The reflective body, narrow ridged screw cap, tapered shoulders, and vertical smartwater branding remain visible and match A in the prior snapshots.

labels.label: B candidate: cap only
labels.evidence: The exposed wide gray cap, protruding side hinge, and metallic collar resemble B. The foreground bag hides the body, so its orange color cannot be verified in this frame.

trials.review: A is supported by multiple visible distinguishing features. B is a plausible candidate because of the characteristic cap and metallic collar, but its previously distinctive orange body is occluded. The orange printing on the foreground bag is not evidence of the hidden bottle color. Position alone is not used to confirm identity.

retries.error: Camera reported stalled during startup; no image accepted.
retries.recovery: Camera resumed delivering frames without a device restart; retry uses an advancing frame ID.

labels.label: A: silver bottle
labels.evidence: The right bottle has the reflective silver body, narrow ridged screw cap, tapered shoulders, and vertical smartwater branding that distinguish A.

labels.label: B: orange bottle
labels.evidence: The left bottle now shows its orange body again, together with the same metallic collar and wide gray hinged cap seen before and during occlusion.

trials.review: B was uncertain when only its cap was exposed in trial 3. The newly visible orange body provides distinguishing evidence again, together with the unchanged cap and collar. A retains its silver body and branding. The matches use appearance rather than position.

feedback.scope: initial small-text viewer, after the first two measured trials
feedback.reported: It says expired right now, I have seen labels change but it is not really readable and does not match to each bottle when both are in view.
feedback.interpretation: Screenshot and frame commit prove software rendering, not readable optical presentation. The fixed-list viewer was not designed for physical object alignment.

feedback.scope: large-text viewer after trial-01; not a separate per-trial rating
feedback.reported: Readable, but the labels are not really lined up with the display as much as I would hope, it would be nice if it was similar how to the bounding box of the capture image worked.
feedback.object_alignment: unsatisfactory; fixed list is not object-aligned
feedback.interpretation: Larger text was reported readable. Simultaneous font, duration and side-cue changes are not a controlled comparison. No calibrated physical alignment was implemented.
